anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

apparatus: Insertions <νοητῆς>, α<ἴ>ρειν. Continues Witte p.132 / PDF 136.

bible_refs.note: Moses commanded not to have a shoe.
Take nothing except a staff — Origen's 'not to take a staff' follows the Matthew/Luke form.

pass_a_gloss: And so that we may see the likeness of the law toward the gospel, we shall set beside the things said law-wise also things from gospel things. Moses, being about to lead the people out from Egypt so that he may lead them into the holy land, taking commandments of God, is commanded not to have a shoe; and the apostles, being sent to lead out from the intelligible Egypt the people from nations, are commanded not to take a staff into a road, nor a bag nor to have sandals bound on.
pass_b_english: And so that we may see the likeness of the law to the gospel, we shall set beside the things said according to the law also things from the gospel. Moses, about to lead the people out of Egypt in order to bring them into the holy land, receiving commandments of God, is commanded not to have a shoe. And the apostles, being sent to lead the people from the nations out of intelligible Egypt, are commanded not to take a staff for the road, nor a bag, nor to have sandals bound on (Exodus 3:5) (Matthew 10:10) (Luke 9:3) (Luke 10:4) (Mark 6:8).
source_text: Ἵνα δὲ τὴν ὁμοιότ[η]τα τοῦ νόμου τὴν πρὸς τὸ εὐ[α]γγέλιον ἴδωμεν, τὰ νομ[ίμ]ως εἰρημένα καὶ ἐξ εὐαγγε[λι]κῶν παραθησόμεθα. Μω[ϋσ]ῆς τὸν λαὸν μέλλων ἐξ[αγα]γεῖν ἐξ Αἰγύπτου, ἵνα εἰς τὴ[ν ἁ]γίαν γῆν εἰσάξῃ ἐντολὰς θ(εο)ῦ λαμβάνων, κελεύεται ὑπόδημα μὴ ἔχειν, καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἀποστελλόμενοι ἐξᾶξαι ἀπὸ τῆς <νοητῆς> Αἰγύπτου τὸν ἐξ ἐθνῶν λαὸν κελεύονται μὴ ῥάβδον α<ἴ>ρειν εἰς ὁδόν, μὴ πήραν μηδὲ σανδάλια ὑποδεδέσθαι.
